title: Staged cutover crossfade coordinator for runtime ↔ API rollout
creator: Ava Martinez
body: Purpose: coordinate a deterministic, observable crossfade that shifts traffic and capabilities between legacy runtime endpoints and new runtime-API split surfaces across regions. Scope: runtime, console routing layers, API gateway config, rollout calendar, and fallback lanes for Dedicated/Private customers. Goals: (1) keep 99.9% availability during cutover windows, (2) bound tail latency regressions to +10% for p95, (3) verify feature parity for structured output and function-calling in each cohort, (4) complete regional cutover for NA/EU/APAC within the release window. Approach: define per-region pulse windows (preflight, smoke, ramp, observation), automated traffic weights via feature flags, emergency kill-switches (circuit-breaker routes), and a coordinated observability dashboard that surfaces model-variant divergence and token-cost delta by route. Success metrics: per-region error-rate delta <= 0.2pp, rollout completion < 5 business days per region, rollback incidence = 0. First milestones: alignment workshop with Eng/Infra/SRE (complete), production canary plan (draft), console routing feature-flag runbook (in review). Risks & mitigations: kernel scheduling mismatch — mitigate with canary traffic pinned to low-impact tenants; KV cache warmup causing latency spike — mitigate with pre-warm traffic and staged batching config. Required artifacts: cutover runbook (Confluence), canary dashboards (Grafana), PR set for gateway configs (GitHub), and postmortem template. Owners: PM lead (Ava Martinez) overall; Eng lead (Liam Chen) rollout execution; SRE on-call rotation for each region. Communication plan: daily standups during active cutover, pre/post-run email to cohort owners, and a consumer-facing status page update if SLA risk detected.
